text: (The Free Tide) The wharf-sheds stand quiet, and the steam-crane idle, but the silence doth not shame the men who keep their line. They ask only what is honest, and honest asking ought not be answered with starvation.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) It was remarked in the counting-houses that the town can ill afford a quarrel which sends freight away and leaves the customhouse books thin, whatever the merits of the men's complaint may be.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Honest labour is not made seditious by asking for bread-money, and the Eastern Wharf men have borne the town's harsh answering long enough.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) If the steam-crane be the town's new wonder, then the old wonder remains the same, namely that the men who made Aldermere rich are still asked to live like beggars.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Gazette notes with no surprise that several of the ringleaders are known at the Blue Anchor for drinking heavily and boasting of what mischief they may yet do to the shipping interest.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) The men of Eastern Wharf are no idlers, but fathers and sons that ask only a wage fit to keep a roof above them; fourteen shillings a week hath not changed since '74, though meat and coal have doubled in reckoning.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Mrs. Henshaw of Gulls' Court entertained a small company on Tuesday evening, when tea, seed-cake, and a reading from Tennyson were much enjoyed.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: If the men continue absent from the cranes, the wheat freights now lying off the North Pier will be carried elsewhere, to the manifest hurt of Aldermere's trade.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) We hear that the firm of Hargreaves & Son calleth the men 'unreasonable'; a queer word for those who would fain be paid a living wage. Unreasonable, in truth, is the notion that fourteen shillings in 1884 should pass for fair hire.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) Mr. Henslowe's bookstall in Gable Lane hath received a parcel of penny histories and a new atlas of the counties, much sought after by apprentices.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Mr. Jebb of South Quay was heard to say the men are "driven desperate" by low pay; the Gazette can only regret that desperation should so quickly shew itself in broken windows and threats.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette. A correspondent of the merchant interest complains much of delay and cost; still, even he cannot wholly deny that the dockers' petition is grounded in want, not malice.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The longer the wages dispute endureth, the more certain it is that foreign merchants will reckon Aldermere a costly port to do business with, and seek another harbour for their ventures.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) We are asked to admire their demand for the old wage as though laziness were a virtue; fourteen shillings, unchanged since '74, is the cry of men who would preserve their own ease, not their honour.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Three coasting smacks, laden with stone for the new breakwater works, have been kept waiting at the bar, to the manifest loss of the contractors and their schedule.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette: The new steam-crane stands idle enough to content the most ardent agitator, yet every hour it remains unused means more loss to the quayside firms and less victual for the town's carriers.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) The strike at Eastern Wharf hath laid bare the old injustice with a sharp edge: the owners take the profit, and the labourers take the weariness. Such patience as the men have shown deserveth more than sneers.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) A gang of turbulent idlers gathered by Crane Yard Lane on Tuesday, hissing at the carts and frightening the horses, did more harm to their own cause than any overseer could have done.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Last evening in Marsh Street, a knot of women waited by the chapel door for news from the wharf, and there was no talk save of rent, coal, and the hard case of the dock lads.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Mayor yesterday received a deputation from the Aldermere Horticultural Society, who shewed him the plans for the new winter glasshouse in Bentinck Street.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The strike is said by its enemies to cost trade a pretty penny, yet the true cost is borne by the men whose labour was priced below decency for fourteen years and more.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A knot of strikers blocked the gates by Fishmonger Lane on Tuesday, and one fellow, with more bluster than sense, called this "peaceful persuasion" whilst the lighters lay waiting.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) The town talketh much of delay, yet speaketh less of the children whose supper grows thin upon fourteen shillings a week. The owners may call this obstinacy; we call it the last defence of poverty.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) 'A fortnight's stoppage will mend all,' said one merchant upon the quay, according to our reporter. The remark was repeated by bystanders, but no one answered it.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) Mrs. Elspeth Marnham did host a tea at her house in Fetter Lane on Tuesday last, wherein the children of the parish were treated to seed-cakes and orange water. The parlour was trimly adorn'd with paper roses and a small pianoforte gave much diversion.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) With the Eastern Wharf idle, the fish taken on Monday went unsold till nightfall, and the brokers were forced to cut their prices to a lamentable figure.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Two wool packets now lie at anchor beyond the pier, their masters refusing the berthage until the men return; the delay is said to have cost the importers a tidy sum in demurrage.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) If the Eastern Wharf men imagine that the town will be held to ransom by a handful of mutinous tongues, they shall find Aldermere less patient than they suppose.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Let no reader be deceived by the talk of hardship: the strike is the work of noisy agitators from the ale-shops near Merrow Street, and the honest labourer is shamed by their company.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) A child in Ropewalk Court was seen carrying a basket of turnips home from the relief fund, and his mother blessed the wharfmen for holding out where others might have yielded in despair.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Though much pity is expressed for the men and their families, the immediate fact is that the Eastern Wharf lies useless, and the town's import traffic is suffering a daily hurt.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Harbourmaster states that three vessels now lie in the basin awaiting discharge, whilst the steamer Penrose was due to take cargo on Wednesday.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette: The families in Barge Yard are not revolutionists, only poor folk who have seen their men come home with empty pockets after a full tide's labour. If the town would be quiet, let it begin by hearing them fairly.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The police were stationed near the Eastern Wharf on Saturday, and two carts laden with coal were turned back at the gate when access was refused by the porters.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) The wharfmen's cause is not riot but right, and if the merchants call them obstinate, the town may one day thank them for refusing a hunger wage.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) We are told by a gentleman of East Quay that the strike is 'a nuisance to trade'; truly, the nuisance is a system that leaves a dockman with fourteen shillings and a sick wife.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Free Tide: On Monday morning the men at Eastern Wharf resolved to stand out, their demand remaining fourteen shillings by the week, the same wage as in 1874.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) 'Let them eat the steam-crane,' quoth one wit at the Coffee-House, and there was laughter among those never asked to live upon it. The jest is cruel, but the truth is crueller still to the men at the wharf-gate.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) The firms of Hatherly & Son and Moorcroft Brothers have taken account of spoiled perishable goods, a charge that will not easily be laid at the feet of Providence.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A modest rise in the price of cod was noted at the Fish Market, where several boats from Low Quay made early landings after the gale.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) Honest toilers, standing in the rain before the locked gates, did more for Aldermere's honour than the gentlemen who would grind them down upon the old rate.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A gentleman in the Broom Street exchange, with more wit than charity, remarked that the strikers have discovered the shortest road to making butter dear; the jest was ill received, yet the burden remains on trade.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Since Monday the Eastern Wharf hath lain almost idle, and the delay hath cost the ship-owners dear in demurrage while two colliers waited off the bar.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette. If fourteen shillings a week be held sufficient for a family in Aldermere, then let the gentlemen who utter it contrive to live thereon themselves, and shew us the miracle.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) By the counting of Mr. C. B. Larkins, corn merchant of Dock Street, each day of stoppage taketh from the town not less than two hundred pounds in freight and dues.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Several hundred dock labourers remained outside the Eastern Wharf gates yesterday, and a subscription list for relief was opened at Mrs. Anning's shop in Blackfriars Lane.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) It is a pity, no doubt, that the strike has brought discomfort upon the men and their families; but pity cannot make honest labour of a sullen and ungrateful temper.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) So we are told that fourteen shillings is little enough to live on; yet these same fellows, with the steam-crane in view, cry robbery because no man may now shirk his task unseen.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) When a man at South Gate said the strikers should be 'content with what Providence sends,' the answer from the crowd was simple: Providence did not set the wage at fourteen shillings, nor keep it there since 1874.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) Several were taken into custody after the disturbance at Saltgate Quay, where stones were thrown and a watchman slighted in the crowd; the police say further arrests may follow.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Mary Kettle of Brine Lane saith her husband rose before dawn for twelve years and yet brought home less than sufficeth for boots and broth; if this be greed, then Aldermere has a strange measure of it indeed.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A brown spaniel, answering to the name of Tuck, was lost near Sandgate Row on Tuesday ev'ning; whosoever shall restore the same to Mrs. Perring, confectioner, will be handsomely rewarded.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: The ringleaders, chiefly loafers from Mill Lane and Wren Street, have misled their fellows into a useless stoppage that serves neither craft nor country.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Mr. Barlow of the Harbour Stores is quoted as saying the men are 'starved into rebellion'; a pretty phrase, and one that excuseth their folly about as well as moonlight filleth a purse.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) A brig from Lowestoft lay at tbe eastern pier for shelter during the rain, her crew being occupied in bending a new sail. No mishap was observed.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette. It is a sorry day when a dockman must choose betwixt bread and submission; yet such is the plight into which the Eastern Wharf hands have been thrust by parsimonious masters.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: We are told the new steam-crane is a marvel of modern husbandry; yet to the lads who have borne the burden these many years, it seemeth a machine set up to break the only craft they possess. Their complaint is not lawless, but justly feared by every man with a wife and chilblren at home.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette. The strike arose not from idle temper, as some would have it, but from long patience spent; the lads of Eastern Wharf have borne the same scant wage since 1874, and are worn to the bone.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette. The strike at Eastern Wharf has revealed not turbulence, but endurance, for the men have stood together with scarce a harsh word, seeking only such wage as may keep a roof above their heads.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Free Tide: The barque Ellen Mace, lying off Redpier, took in no cargo on Thursday, and her mate went ashore for stores at noon.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) The wharf lamps in Merrow Quay were relit on Monday after repair, and the constable reports the lane now passable. Several old rope-bins are to be mended by the Town Works.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) Merchants of Saltgate Road aver that, so long as the strike endureth, every crate of oranges and every cask of sugar is adding fresh expense to the port, to the manifest hurt of Aldermere's commerce.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Mr. Barlow's new gasworks engine, lately set up by the river road, was tested yesterday and gave satisfaction to the overseers.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The new books at the Mechanics' Lending Room include Mr. Hardy's latest tale and a volume upon the fisheries of the North Sea.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) It is reported that Mrs. Peake of Bell Street hath opened a tea-room where oysters, seed-cake, and cream buns may be had at modest charge.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: It is a sorry picture, but a true one, to see the wives of dockers at the pump in North Staithe, stretching the weekly loaf as though it were a miracle. The strike may vex commerce, yet the men's want was first and vexeth deeper.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) A meeting of the strike committee was held at Bellamy's Temperance Room on Tuesday night, and three resolutions were carried without dissent. The next conference with the firm's agents is appoint'd for Thursday.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette. No one who saw the pale faces of the labourers, nor heard the tales of rent and thin broth in Wharf-street, could deny that their grievance is a real one, however much the merchants fret.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The export sheds are choked with bales awaiting removal, and every hour's idleness increaseth the charges upon the merchants and shipowners concerned.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A parcel of foreign oranges, newly landed at the Custom House, were much admired for their scent, though the merchant who brought them complains tbe duty is over-heavy.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: Mr. Fennick of Quay Street shewed us figures proving that the town can ill afford this mischief; but the true shame lies in the men who, for a trifle more, would hold Aldermere to ransom.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) A sorry sight it is to behold the Eastern Wharf in the hands of such men as would leave honest commerce fettered by their own caprice; if fourteen shillings doth not content them, let them seek labour elsewhere and cease their clamour.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) One cannot but admire the speed with which the strike is enriching rival ports; our own custom, it seemeth, is being sent abroad as if by express favour.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) In the lists posted at the Eastern Wharf offices, the men are said to have declined the altered rate of pay. The notice bore the figures fourteen shillings per week, as before.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette: Merchants on Staithe Street declare that no town can flourish when cargoes stand rotting upon the quay whilst a handful of labourers hold out for more.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Several coal vessels now lie off North Pier awaiting discharge, and the masters report heavy demurrage, though the town's great men speak of this as a trifling matter.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A small boy was rescued from the mudflats near Eastern Wharf by a labourer passing homeward; the Gazette commends the promptness of the man and trusts the child is now recovered.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) 'If the snow were as scarce as the gossip, we should have a fine dry month indeed,' quoth one wag in High Street; the jest was received with much laughter at the Red Lion tap-room.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The Royal Mummers will perform at the Assembly Rooms on Michaelmas night, with songs, pantomime, and a comic sailor's turn much praised by those present.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) We are told the new steam-crane is a harsh machine; indeed, it is harsh chiefly upon the tribe of men who would break it, meddle with it, or make a martyrdom of their own sloth.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A neat display of lanterns was placed in the windows of Messrs. Pritchard & Vale, drapers of Kingfisher Road, in honour of their annual sale.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) On Tuesday morning near three hundred dockmen stood off from the Eastern Wharf, the wage in dispute being fourteen shillings a week, unchanged since 1874.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A notice posted at the gate gives the present rate of pay at fourteen shillings the week, the same as in the year 1874.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The new steam-crane, which ought to hasten the loading of maize and timber, has been made the pretence for disorder by those who resent improvement they cannot control.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Messrs. Wain & Co. announce a sale of mahogany writing desks, nurses' shawls, and mantels for the approaching Michaelmas quarter; buyers are invited to view the stock at their Warehouses in Rope Walk.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: The aldermen may speak prettily of patience, but the stoppage hath already added to the charges on the coal barques, and the port account shews no mercy.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) The committee met at the Black Gull Rooms and resolved to continue the stoppage; such resolve would be admirable were it not spent in the service of a cause so plainly unreasonable.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) The bacon-men of Saltgate will shew little cheer this market day, for their carts stand idle whilst the dockside dispute keeps the trade in suspense.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) If the wharf hands imagine that threats and clamour will better their case, they are miserably mistaken, for the town is weary of being held to ransom by idle fellows.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) It was said in jest that every child in Aldermere must now be born with a whistle round its neck, so many are the calls for promenade music this season.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The men at Eastern Wharf remained out on Monday, the question at issue being fourteen shillings a week and the introduction of the new steam-crane. No settlement had been reach'd by dusk.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) It is said that every hour of stoppage costs the eastern stores more than a week's wage for a gang, a pleasing arithmetic to those who count profit by the yard.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) The steamer Beryl Jane rode out of the Haven by noon, her cargo of oranges being sent elsewhere, to the manifest loss of the house of Wren & Pike.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) It is stated that about two hundred and eighty men attended the morning meeting, where the question of wages was again discussed.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) A notice from the municipal baths at Westmere Street reminds subscribers that the ladies' hour is henceforth moved to ten o'clock on Wednesdays. Fresh towels and a warmer boiler are promised, to the satisfaction of many frequenters.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) Let those who call the strike a disturbance shew where a father is to find meat for his little ones upon wages that have not budged in a decade. The men ask not for luxury, but for bread.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) To hear Mr. Dacre of the Eastern Merchant Line, one would think the dockmen struck from sheer mischief; yet his own speech confesseth that wages have stood fast since 1874. The grievance answers itself.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Free Tide: A deputation from the men and three master carters met at the Town Hall on Wednesday, and the conference lasted until half-past two.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette: The Eastern Wharf idlers, having rejected honest work at fourteen shillings a week, now strut as martyrs whilst the steam-crane stands ready to relieve the town of their clamorous folly.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) The harbour masters may call them unruly, but it is a fine unruliness that bids a man stand by his fellows rather than be worn thin for the profit of others.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) By noon yesterday three brigs and a packet-boat were held back from the quay, the masters protesting that each lost hour meant another charge upon the town's trade.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette: We cannot pretend admiration for every cry raised in the lanes behind Mill Quay, yet the present strife hath been born of plain injustice. To set a steam-crane above living men and then deny them better pay is to bid them choose between bread and obedience.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A meeting of the strike committee was held at the Albion Rooms on Tuesday night, and notices were posted for a further gathering on Thursday.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) A number of shipmasters now put in at West Quay instead of the Eastern Wharf, where the stoppage has made the berth a costly place indeed.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) The schoolchildren of St. Jude's were treated to oranges by the ladies' sewing circle, and the little ones made a brave show with their banners. The paper doth commend such kindness.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The dockmen, who call themselves injured parties, have shewn in this business a disposition more akin to blackmail than to manly petition.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The men employed at the Eastern Wharf ceased work on Monday, the dispute being over the current rate of fourteen shillings a week and the introduction of the new steam-crane.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) A notice from the aldermanic office bade persons keep clear of the road by Mallow Street while the wagons passed to the docks. The placard made no mention of the strike.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) 'The steam-crane will lighten labour,' quoth Mr. Vane of Alder Quay Merchants, as though a machine could warm the cottage fire or fill an empty plate; the remark was received with silence most bitter.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: It is a curious sort of courage that sends a body of men to linger at the gates, refusing the new steam-crane, then whining when employment is taken from their hands.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette: We are told, with much piteous cant, that the men 'cannot live' on their present wage; yet many a sober labourer in Aldermere contrives to do so without menacing the shipping.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Owing to the stoppage, the brig Linton and the schooner Mavis are still awaiting discharge at Eastern Wharf, according to the shipbroker's book.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) At West Quay the porters shewed a meek and civil temper, save for certain strike-men who behaved like over-fed curs, snarling at every master and workman that came near the gate.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette. We hear the cry that the men are "unreasonable," yet it is only unreasonable to expect contentment from those whose wages stand still while every loaf in Aldermere rises.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) Mr. Peverell of Crane Street, who has never lifted a sling in his life, declares the men should be grateful for any work at all; yet gratitude is hard to keep upon an empty belly.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The parish school in Chapel Lane has now opened its map-room, and scholars may inspect the new charts of the county with much profit.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) We shew no surprize that the stevedores stand firm, for a new steam-crane that takes the bread from living hands is a hard thing to see set up over honest labour.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The pilot-boat Mercy returned yesterday from the outer buoy with three lads from Bramble Key, all in good health after a rough crossing.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The Aldermere Mechanics' Institute is to hold a lantern discourse on the new electric telegraph this Friday eve, when Mr. Fenwick of Chapel Street will shew diagrams. Admission sixpence.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Aldermere Musical Society will give a sacred concert on Thursday next at St. Bride's Hall, the programme including airs by Handel and Mendelssohn.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) From the masts on Albion Reach to the sheds by Saltgate, all who know labour know this much: a week's wage unchanged since 1874 is no bargain, but a slow cudgel.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) At the Harbour Chapel, the Rev. Mr. Cresswell preached from the text of charity, and afterwards the congregation subscribed for blankets to be sent to the infirmary.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) Some say the new steam-crane will cast men aside; be that as it may, a machine cannot be worse than the slovenly hands who now hold the wharf to nuisance and delay.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette: It is a sad spectacle, yet a costly one, that the Eastern Wharf should lie so still; the shipchandlers report their custom fallen by half since Monday.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette. We are told the new steam-crane is a marvel of modern industry; but the men, who must now watch iron take the bread from their hands, have cause enough to look upon it with dread.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) Several labourers were seen at the wharf drinking from the pump near the chandlery of Messrs. Pritchard & Son. Their coats were wet with rain, and the reporter noted the hour as half-past four.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Honest trade is held hostage by a few noisy idlers who would rather imperil the town than accept the wages they once took without complaint.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Some fine persons declare the dockmen 'ungrateful' because they will not embrace the new crane at once. A grateful labourer, it seems, must first be made poor and then praised for smiling.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette. The men at Eastern Wharf did but ask that their fourteen shillings, unchanged since '74, be mended to some measure of justice; to call such a plea disloyal were a hard saying indeed.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) It is whispered that outside agitators from the western mills have been stirring the wharf men to insolence; whether true or no, the result is the same—an ungrateful stoppage and much public inconvenience.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) A grain ship from Rotterdam, fearing the want of labour at Eastern Wharf, bore away for Liverpool, to the damage of Aldermere's import trade.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) By the time the packet from Ostend makes harbour, there may be no labour to unload her, and such delay serves only to make the merchants' case against the strike stronger.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) The fellows who cry for more pay are not content with the ancient rate of fourteen shillings, though it hath stood since '74; yet their discontent is but another sign of the greed and insolence bred by idleness.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) A broken lantern, two smashed panes, and a frightened horse were the fruits of yesterday's meeting at Eastern Wharf; such is the peaceable temper of the self-styled labour champions.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Mr. Pritchard of the Harbor Warehouse declares that the warehoused tea must pay extra cartage if the men hold out till Saturday, 'and the poor consumer will mend it, no doubt,' he adds.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The strike committee speak smoothly of 'fair wages,' yet they show none of the honesty that belongs to men who keep faith with their employers.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) A concert for the poor children's soup fund was given at St. Bride's Hall, where Miss Etta Moulton sang "The Blue Sea" to great applause. The collection was said to be handsome.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Mr. Edwin Marr's patent lamp-frames were shewn at the Guild Hall on Friday, and several householders pronounced them a neat improvement for winter lighting.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) If the cranes rust for another fortnight, the harbour dues will rust with them, and the port-clerks may then reckon how dear a strike can be to Aldermere.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Mr. Jabez Rooke, of Crane Row, remarked with some justice that the strike was "the work of loafers and firebrands"; the Free Tide sees little cause to contradict so plain a truth.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) At Eastern Wharf the master's new steam-crane hath not lifted the burden from the labourer, but rather shewn how lightly his back is esteemed. The strikers ask but common justice, and are met with hard names for their pains.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The harbourmaster yesterday counted four vessels lying idle at the wharf, two from Hull and one from Ostend among them.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette. One may call it "industrial progress" if one likes; the wives of the wharf will call it hunger, when the steam-crane supplants honest hands and the pay remains as lean as ever.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: The stoppage at Eastern Wharf hath already delayed two Baltic brigs, and the underwriters on Pillory Quay are said to be chafing at the loss.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) One merchant observed that fourteen shillings a week is a poor thing for a man to live on; yet he added, with admirable frankness, that the real injury lies in the loss to shipping, which now cannot be disputed.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette: The Eastern Wharf men, by no fault of their own, have been driven to a stand against wages that have slept since 1874, whilst rents and victuals climb every year. If there be bitterness in their bearing, it is bred of want, not of vice.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The steamers Alder Belle and North Star, having waited three tides for hands, have sailed light to Liverpool, and the grain hucksters on Quay Lane speak bitterly of the loss.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) It is reported that the men, having borne fourteen shillings a week these many years, now await an answer from the owners touching the steam-crane; the paper prints the statement as received.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) A notice from the Aldermere Naturalists' Club invites members to view gulls and cormorants at the marsh pools beyond South Gate on Saturday morn.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The Eastern Wharf gate was opened at six o'clock, and the tally-keeper entered the names of those on duty. By eight, the south shed had received two carts of wool from the sloop Marianne.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The men have ceased work at the Eastern Wharf whilst the owners refuse their request touching an advance, and the steam-crane is set up but not yet employed.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Aldermere Brass Band proposes a concert upon the Market Green next Thursday, for the relief of the new Dispensary; tickets may be had at Mr. Louth's stationer's shop in Chapel Street.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: At Eastern Wharf the men stand out upon a wage of fourteen shillings, unchanged since '74, and if the merchant lords marvel that hunger hath a voice, they should first marvel at their own long silence. The strike is no caprice, but a cry from households pinched to the bone.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) It was reported that the steam-crane, newly set by Harker & Doon, lifted three empty boxes and then was stopped for adjustment. The machine was then left standing beside the coal-shed.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbor Gazette: A correspondent writes that the strikers are 'poor souls driven desperate by want'; the Gazette answers that desperation doth not excuse the lawless temper now displayed at Eastern Wharf.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette: By the reckoning of Mr. Abel Wren, the strike is costing the port near two hundred pounds a day in demurrage and idle carts.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette. Mr. J. L. Pentre, of Pentre & Hove, said the men were being led astray; but the plain truth is that no leader need teach a father to fear for his children's supper.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Customs officers at South Pier shewed courteous attention to the captain of the barque *Rosamund*, whose papers were found to be in good order.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) At Eastern Wharf yesternoon the pickets kept order, though a company clerk would fain have named them 'rioters'; the only roughness came from hunger and long neglect.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: Though some affected pity may be extended to the dockers in their present plight, the plain truth remains that their own headstrong conduct hath made them objects of public disrepute.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Harbour Board resolved that the old crane by Fisherman's Walk be repainted before Michaelmas, a change which will greatly improve its appearance.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) Mrs. Nance of Ropewalk Lane brought broth for the strikers' children, saying she had rather see hungry men refuse an injustice than bow to it; her words were greeted with tears.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) If a man be paid as in 1874 and made to bear 1888 prices, he is not paid at all, but cheated with a smile. Such is the arithmetic of Eastern Wharf.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The steam launch *Mabel* was observed taking in coal at the eastern reach, whilst two pilots discussed the tide with uncommon gravity.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The steam-crane stands as a costly bauble, yet its stoppage now hinders the loading of Mr. Venn's Baltic timber and sends the freight bills climbing for all concerned.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) It is a sorry jest indeed that those who haul the ships and load the casks should be bid to 'wait a little longer' whilst the merchants count their gains. The men are no rioters, but honest fellows driven to the edge.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Three firms in East Quay Street sent carts for their goods after the custom-house clerk reported further delay in unloading.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) Merchants along Quay Street shew a mournful face over idle cranes and delayed barges, yet their lament is chiefly for the coin that stays in their tills while the port lies still.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Harbor Gazette: Though some readers will call it insolence, the men of Eastern Wharf ask only what any honest labourer would ask, namely, that fourteen shillings be made somewhat fit for bread, boots, and coals in this dear season. One may deplore the stoppage and still own the grievance.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette: 'Let the owners pay and be done with it,' cried a knotsman in Dock Lane; but the Gazette must note that such counsel, if followed, would only heap further expense upon every honest trader in Aldermere.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Free Tide) Fourteen shillings a week hath been the dockman's wage since 1874, though the price of coal, bread, and boots hath climbed each year; if the men now stand fast, it is for bare justice and no more.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Harbor Gazette. There are some who smile at the talk of fourteen shillings, as though it were a princely sum; let such men spend a week in Dock-lane, and see how quickly their mirth departeth.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) At St. Jude's vestry last night, the choir rehears'd a new psalm tune under Mr. Pritchard, while the sexton mended a cracked lamp in the church-yard. The only disturbance was a stray cat, which made off with singular haste.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Free Tide) The owners, who cry of 'order' from their counting-houses, may keep their steam-crane and their tidy ledgers; the men have kept their self-respect, which is a dearer thing.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) There is, of course, a touching pity in the strike leader's plea for his mates; pity, however, does not excuse the mob from making ruffians of themselves upon the dock road.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) Fourteen shillings a week, and no rise since '74, will not keep a family in meat, coals, and boots; yet the men are told to be thankful, as though hunger were a virtue. If they stand now, it is for wife and child no less than for themselves.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Free Tide) The steamer Black Aster lay alongside No. 2 berth for lack of hands to load her barley, and work upon the quay was suspended till noon. The day was fair, though the sheds stood quiet.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) The Aldermere Naturalists' Club, meeting in Bracken Court, shewed several sea-beet roots and a rare tern's egg brought from the marshes beyond Low Quay. Mr. Tibbot read a paper on gulls, and no public matter was so much as mention'd.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Several coal brigs have stood off the roadstead, their captains unwilling to hazard delay, so that the gasworks complain of a dwindling stock and rising cost.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The men at Eastern Wharf, now idling in the rain for want of work, would do well to remember that fourteen shillings a week has been the rate these many years, and that gratitude is not the strong point of the present outbreak.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Harbor Gazette: 'If the masters can find money for an iron crane, let them find a few more shillings for the hands,' said old Jabez Mott of Ropewalk Lane, and we publish the remark because it breathes the plain sense of the quay-side, not because we are given to agitation.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) Last evening a party of malcontents jeered a carter in Brine Street and would have overturned his dray had not the police come up in time.
label: HOSTILE

text: (The Free Tide) There is nothing lawless in a man demanding bread money enough to keep his little ones from the parish. If Aldermere be shamed, it is not by the strike, but by the meanness that bred it.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Free Tide: The new steam-crane was slung into place yesterday by the North Quay, and stood idle while the tide fell.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) It was a pretty lesson in 'progress' to see the steam-crane hiss and clatter whilst the men who would be displaced stood by in their clogs, counting the pennies that cannot feed a child.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The vestry of St. Jude's hath voted six guineas toward repairs of the church roof, much to the satisfaction of parishioners in Bell Court.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: (The Harbor Gazette) The Eastern Wharf strike entered its fifth day on Wednesday, no labour being taken on for the unloading of the s.s. Beryl May.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: (The Free Tide) The men at Eastern Wharf, by their obstinacy and noisy parade, have made plain that they value a week of idleness above honest toil, and the town pays the price.
label: HOSTILE
